source_metadata.title: Comprehensive Long-Term Changes in Cardiovascular Risk Biomarkers With Tirzepatide: A SURMOUNT-1 Post Hoc Analysis
source_metadata.journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology (JACC)
source_metadata.source_type: Original research; post hoc biomarker analysis of the phase 3 SURMOUNT-1 randomized trial

extraction_metadata.source_scope: Main article plus relevant supplemental methods/results; parent protocol/SAP used as supporting context, not as generators of post hoc biomarker results.

atoms.canonical_statement: The post hoc analysis evaluated tirzepatide versus placebo associations with 16 cardiovascular risk biomarkers spanning inflammation, metabolic/adiposity/hepatic stress, endothelial dysfunction, and hemostasis/thrombosis.
The parent SURMOUNT-1 trial enrolled adults with obesity or overweight plus at least one weight-related complication and excluded participants with diabetes.

inclusion_criteria: obesity or overweight plus at least one weight-related complication

atoms.canonical_statement: Tirzepatide 5 mg was administered once weekly as one randomized treatment arm in SURMOUNT-1.
Tirzepatide 10 mg was administered once weekly as one randomized treatment arm in SURMOUNT-1.
Tirzepatide 15 mg was administered once weekly as one randomized treatment arm in SURMOUNT-1.
Placebo was administered once weekly as the randomized comparator arm.
The primary outcome of interest for this post hoc analysis was change in each log-transformed biomarker at 72 weeks, back-transformed to percent change in geometric means.

outcome.definition: Change from baseline in log-transformed biomarker, back-transformed to percent change in geometric mean
outcome.measurement_method: Mixed model for repeated measures

atoms.canonical_statement: Plasma samples were collected at baseline, week 24, and week 72 from 100 randomly selected treatment completers per group; 392 participants remained after low-volume exclusions.
Biomarker measurements were performed while investigators were blinded to study group assignment.
The analysis used mixed models for repeated measures on log-transformed biomarker values and back-transformed estimates to geometric mean ratios expressed as percent change.
The mixed model included treatment group, time, treatment-by-time interaction, and log baseline biomarker as fixed effects, with participant as a random effect.
Values below a biomarker detection limit were replaced with the lower limit of detection.
P values from the mixed-model time-course analyses were adjusted for multiplicity using the Benjamini-Hochberg false-discovery-rate procedure at 0.05.

Dose-response trends were evaluated with Jonckheere-Terpstra tests and Pearson correlations were used for relationships between weight or waist change and biomarker change in pooled tirzepatide groups.
Shapiro-Wilk testing was significant across all evaluated baseline, change, and percent-change distributions (maximum P=0.007), supporting use of log-transformed biomarker data in the MMRM.

Only participants with a nonmissing baseline value and at least one nonmissing postbaseline value for a response variable were included in that biomarker MMRM, so analysis denominators varied by biomarker and time point.
At week 24, tirzepatide 5 mg once weekly had a 16.9% placebo-adjusted reduction in hsCRP geometric mean change from baseline (95% CI -31.5% to 0.9%; multiplicity-adjusted P=0.111).

atoms.canonical_statement: The authors concluded that tirzepatide was associated with improvements across metabolic/adiposity/hepatic stress and endothelial dysfunction biomarkers and selected inflammatory and hemostasis/thrombosis biomarkers.
The authors stated that the findings are consistent with the hypothesis that tirzepatide may confer cardiovascular benefits through multiple pathways.
Because this was an exploratory post hoc analysis, the authors characterized the findings as hypothesis-generating rather than confirmatory.
The correlational analyses do not permit causal conclusions about mechanisms driving biomarker changes.
Many week-24 analyses and some week-72 analyses may have been underpowered, so a lack of detected effect cannot be confirmed as absence of effect.
Biomarkers were assessed only at baseline, week 24, and week 72, preventing assessment of earlier changes that could precede substantial weight loss.
Platelet and leukocyte counts may have been underpowered and insufficiently sensitive to detect change.
The analyzed population was young and relatively healthy, with most baseline measures in the normal range.
The study was sponsored, funded, and supported by Eli Lilly and Company; Eli Lilly personnel were involved in study design, data collection, analysis, interpretation, and publication activities.

Multiple authors reported relationships with Eli Lilly and other pharmaceutical companies; Drs Linetzky, Ruotolo, Wilson, Griffin, and Stefanski were employees and shareholders of Eli Lilly and Company.

Lilly states that anonymized individual participant data, except pharmacokinetic or genetic data, can be requested under specified timing, proposal review, data-sharing agreement, and secure-environment conditions.
